accepted_edits.reason: Edits answer reasoning-1, reasoning-2 and done_when-1 on §14 and §15

findings.reason: the endpoint must distinguish an ordinary resume (delivery intended) from a reopen that starts a new attempt after the subject completed, or the node removes a documented, deliberate mechanism to satisfy the gate.
findings.text: s15's deliverable "A refused advice is never delivered to a later attempt" contradicts the delivery the tree intends at the very file it cites: resumption.py:128-134 states the text "is kept beside the run's resume records and delivered to the next resume of that run", and dispatch_sessions.py:1330-1336 prepends it to the next resume's advice on purpose, while s15's blanket rule would license a node to delete that path — so an ordinary resume would stop carrying an answer the operator gave to the attempt that holds the run

findings.reason: the stated mechanism is refuted by its own anchor, so a node reading the section looks for a rename step that does not exist and may fix the wrong site.
findings.text: s15's Why says the refused advice was "renamed to resume-3-advice.txt", but nothing renames it: REFUSED_ADVICE_NAME exists precisely because, as the comment at resumption.py:131-134 says, "a resume-<n>-advice.txt is named for a turn the refused attempt never reached, so its number is unknown at refusal time", and the file is consumed and written into the next attempt's resume-<turn>-advice.txt at launch

findings.reason: without a case that forces the refusal, the half of the deliverable that replaces today's uninformative duty is unmeasured, and the obligation could still name nothing when dispatch fails.
findings.text: s14's deliverable has two branches ("reviewed by the reflex, or the obligation names why the reflex did not and what to run"), but its done-when states two cases for the first branch only and its declared negative control (base revision, repair delivery) exercises no failure at all, so a node can pass by making both deliveries dispatch and never force a dispatch failure

response_events.note: §15 now keeps the deliberate delivery of a refused advice to the next resume and targets the defect: a reopen launches no worker by itself, and its output names any pending advice the next resume will carry.
§15's Why now says the refused advice was consumed into attempt 4's resume-3-advice.txt at the reopen's launch, not renamed.
§14 adds a case that forces the reflex's dispatch to fail and requires the obligation to name the refusal and the command, and its negative control is that case at base.

done_when-1.note: §14 adds a case that forces the reflex's dispatch to fail and requires the obligation to name the refusal and the command, and its negative control is that case at base.

reasoning-1.note: §15 now keeps the deliberate delivery of a refused advice to the next resume and targets the defect: a reopen launches no worker by itself, and its output names any pending advice the next resume will carry.

reasoning-2.note: §15's Why now says the refused advice was consumed into attempt 4's resume-3-advice.txt at the reopen's launch, not renamed.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — resumption.py:135 resolves to REFUSED_ADVICE_NAME, the three cited run ids exist under ~/.config/reckon/crew/runs, 9ed2768368 and 425cb1ef56 resolve, and the s13 evidence fragment exists; the two module names absent from the tree (reckon/crew/reflex.py, reckon/crew/run_commands_resume.py) are hedged in the plan ("if that is where the pass lives", "or the module holding the reopen verb") and are not findings.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s14's naming branch has no test case, so the node can pass without it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections put gate logs under the run directory with a revision header, the literal command and a closing EXIT= line, and neither writes to a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new sections carry no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers into code, and their prose states mechanisms rather than changelog narration.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s15's rule is wider than the defect and its cited line refutes its own account of the mechanism.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s14 and s15 each state one endpoint ("no silent unreviewed delivery", "a reopen never launches on a refused advice"), and each done-when measures that endpoint rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the document's plan-level edges are unchanged and each resolves (depends-on worker-death-is-recorded, informs scoring-should-stop-a-promotion, empty blocks after the earlier removal); the two new sections declare no edge the plan needs.
